body: When the Bell V-22 Osprey entered service in 2007, it became the first operational tiltrotor aircraft, combining the vertical-flight flexibility of a helicopter with the speed and endurance of a fixed-wing aircraft. The transition between the two modes depends on a carefully controlled speed range known as the conversion corridor: according to Global Security, the corridor runs from 40 to 120 knots, and the engine nacelles rotate in 30-degree increments between 90 degrees in helicopter mode and 0 degrees in airplane mode, with a graduated scale of recommended speeds for each angle.

The limits are set by aerodynamic stall: as the nacelles tilt forward they produce less vertical lift, so the wings must take over. The wings need a steady airflow of at least 60 to 80 knots to begin generating partial lift, and flying below that speed while tilting forward will cause the aircraft to sink rapidly. In full airplane mode the V-22 needs roughly 130 to 140 knots just to stay airborne, and attempting to fly at 140 knots with the nacelles still at 60 degrees would impose immense drag on the tilted proprotors; only once airspeed safely clears 140 knots will the flight computer allow the nacelles to lock fully down to 0 degrees for high-speed cruise at 240 to 280 knots.

Slowing down for a vertical landing reverses the procedure and carries its own risks, including vortex ring state, in which an aircraft descending too quickly sinks into its own rotor wash and can roll uncommanded, a mishap that caused fatal crashes during the V-22's development, when 30 service members died between 1991 and 2000, including 19 Marines in a 2000 vortex-ring-state crash. Later accidents kept the safety debate alive: five Marines died in a June 2022 drivetrain crash, and eight US Air Force crew died in a 2023 CV-22 crash caused by metal contamination in the main gearbox, after which the global fleet was grounded until a fix was rolled out. The US Army's successor, the Bell V-280 Valor, designated the MV-75 Cheyenne II, is meant to simplify the design by tilting only the prop rotors and their shafts rather than the entire engine nacelle.
en.summary: The V-22 Osprey's shift from helicopter to airplane flight must stay inside a narrow conversion corridor, with the safe speed range changing at every nacelle angle.
en.title: Why the V-22 Osprey can only change between helicopter and airplane flight within a narrow speed range

body: 貝爾V-22魚鷹式傾斜旋翼機於2007年服役，是航空史上首款投入使用的傾斜旋翼機，兼具直升機的垂直飛行彈性與定翼機的速度與續航力。兩種模式之間的轉換仰賴嚴格控制的速度範圍，也就是所謂的轉換走廊：據Global Security資料，走廊介於40至120節，發動機短艙以30度為級距，在直升機模式的90度與飛機模式的0度之間轉動，每個角度都有相應的建議速度。
速度限制由氣動失速決定：短艙向前傾斜時垂直升力減少，機翼必須接手。機翼需要至少60至80節的穩定氣流才開始產生部分升力，低於這個速度向前傾斜會使飛機急速下沉；進入全飛機模式後，V-22至少需要約130至140節才能維持飛行，若在短艙仍處60度時就以140節飛行，傾斜的旋翼將承受巨大阻力，只有當空速安全超過140節，飛控電腦才會允許短艙完全鎖定至0度，進入240至280節的高速巡航。

減速垂直降落是反向程序，風險也更高，包括渦環狀態：飛機下降過快時會沉入自身旋翼下洗流，可能導致非指令滾轉；這類事故在V-22研發期間造成致命墜機，1991年至2000年間共30名官兵喪生，其中包括2000年一起渦環狀態墜機中的19名陸戰隊員。其後事故仍讓安全爭議延續：2022年6月一起傳動系統事故造成5名陸戰隊員喪生，2023年一起CV-22墜機因主齒輪箱金屬汙染造成8名美國空軍組員喪生，全球機隊隨後停飛直到修正措施推出。美國陸軍的後繼機種貝爾V-280「Valor」已命名為MV-75「Cheyenne II」，改為只傾斜旋翼與傳動軸而非整個發動機短艙，以簡化設計。
zh.summary: V-22魚鷹式從直升機模式轉換為飛機模式時，必須保持在狹窄的轉換走廊內，安全速度範圍會隨短艙角度而變化。
zh.title: 為什麼V-22魚鷹式只能在嚴格控制的速度範圍內轉換飛行模式
